# 1. Introduction
This analysis develops and evaluates multiple linear regression models to predict monthly rental prices in Tokyo's 23 wards, progressively incorporating additional features and more complex relationships.



# 2. Libraries
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```



# 3. Load Data
```{r load_data}
# Load the preprocessed training dataset
processed_train <- read.csv(
  "processed_train_data.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM"
)


# Load the preprocessed test dataset
processed_test <- read.csv(
  "processed_test_data.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM"
)


# Load the sample submission file
sample_submit <- read.csv(
  "sample_submit.csv",
  header = FALSE
)
```



# 4. Regression Model Development
## 4.1 Train-Validation Split
```{r train_validation_split}
set.seed(123)

train_index <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(processed_train)),
  size = floor(0.8 * nrow(processed_train))
)

train_df <- processed_train[train_index, ]
valid_df <- processed_train[-train_index, ]
```


## 4.2 Data Preparation
```{r model_refinement}
# Group infrequent categories
group_categories <- function(train, valid, col, new_col,
                             min_count, exclude = character()) {

  train_values <- as.character(train[[col]])
  valid_values <- as.character(valid[[col]])

  train_values[is.na(train_values)] <- "missing"
  valid_values[is.na(valid_values)] <- "missing"

  counts <- table(train_values)

  rare <- names(counts[counts <= min_count])
  grouped <- unique(c(rare, exclude))

  train_values[train_values %in% grouped] <- "other"

  valid_values[
    valid_values %in% grouped |
      !(valid_values %in% names(counts))
  ] <- "other"

  train[[new_col]] <- train_values
  valid[[new_col]] <- valid_values

  list(train = train, valid = valid)
}


# Impute numerical missing values
impute_numeric <- function(train, valid, cols) {

  for (col in cols) {

    median_value <- median(train[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)

    if (!is.finite(median_value)) {
      stop(paste("Cannot calculate median for:", col))
    }

    missing_col <- paste0(col, "_missing")

    train[[missing_col]] <- as.integer(is.na(train[[col]]))
    valid[[missing_col]] <- as.integer(is.na(valid[[col]]))

    train[[col]][is.na(train[[col]])] <- median_value
    valid[[col]][is.na(valid[[col]])] <- median_value
  }

  list(train = train, valid = valid)
}


# Align categorical values with training data
align_categories <- function(train, valid, cols) {

  for (col in cols) {

    train[[col]] <- as.character(train[[col]])
    valid[[col]] <- as.character(valid[[col]])

    train[[col]][is.na(train[[col]])] <- "missing"
    valid[[col]][is.na(valid[[col]])] <- "missing"

    train_levels <- unique(train[[col]])
    unknown <- !(valid[[col]] %in% train_levels)

    if (any(unknown)) {

      if (col == "building_structure" && "その他" %in% train_levels) {
        valid[[col]][unknown] <- "その他"

      } else if ("other" %in% train_levels) {
        valid[[col]][unknown] <- "other"

      } else {
        stop(paste("Unknown category in:", col))
      }
    }
  }

  list(train = train, valid = valid)
}
  

# Combine preprocessing steps
prepare_cv_data <- function(train, valid) {

  # Group stations
  data <- group_categories(
    train, valid,
    "station_1", "station_1_grouped", 5
  )

  # Group towns
  data <- group_categories(
    data$train, data$valid,
    "town", "town_grouped_18", 10,
    exclude = c("南千住", "佃")
  )

  # Group layouts
  data <- group_categories(
    data$train, data$valid,
    "layout", "layout_grouped", 5
  )

  train <- data$train
  valid <- data$valid

  # Impute numeric variables
  data <- impute_numeric(
    train, valid,
    c(
      "building_age",
      "floor",
      "total_floor",
      "burner_count",
      "walk_2",
      "walk_3"
    )
  )

  train <- data$train
  valid <- data$valid

  # Handle missing categorical values
  for (col in c("stove_type", "parking_status")) {
    train[[col]][is.na(train[[col]])] <- "missing"
    valid[[col]][is.na(valid[[col]])] <- "missing"
  }

  # Group bicycle parking categories
  train$bicycle_parking_grouped <- as.character(
    train$bicycle_parking_status
  )

  valid$bicycle_parking_grouped <- as.character(
    valid$bicycle_parking_status
  )

  for (dataset in c("train", "valid")) {
    x <- get(dataset)$bicycle_parking_grouped

    x[is.na(x)] <- "missing"
    x[x %in% c("nearby", "unavailable")] <- "other"

    if (dataset == "train") {
      train$bicycle_parking_grouped <- x
    } else {
      valid$bicycle_parking_grouped <- x
    }
  }

  # Handle missing contract information
  train$fixed_term[is.na(train$fixed_term)] <- 0
  valid$fixed_term[is.na(valid$fixed_term)] <- 0
  
  # Handle missing building structure
  train$building_structure <- as.character(train$building_structure)
  valid$building_structure <- as.character(valid$building_structure)
  
  train$building_structure[
    is.na(train$building_structure)
  ] <- "その他"
  
  valid$building_structure[
    is.na(valid$building_structure)
  ] <- "その他"

  # Align categorical levels
  align_categories(
    train,
    valid,
    c(
      "station_1_grouped",
      "town_grouped_18",
      "layout_grouped",
      "stove_type",
      "parking_status",
      "bicycle_parking_grouped",
      "ward",
      "building_structure"
    )
  )
}


# Apply preprocessing
model_data <- prepare_cv_data(
  train_df,
  valid_df
)

train_model_df <- model_data$train
valid_model_df <- model_data$valid
```


## 4.3 Initial Regression Models
```{r}
# Model 1: Basic property characteristics
model_1 <- lm(
  rent ~ area + building_age + floor + total_floor + walk_1,
  data = train_model_df
)


# Model 2: Add location and building characteristics
model_2 <- update(
  model_1,
  . ~ . + ward + layout_grouped + building_structure
)


# Model 3: Add housing facilities
has_vars <- grep("^has_", names(train_model_df), value = TRUE)

model_3 <- update(
  model_2,
  as.formula(
    paste(". ~ . +", paste(has_vars, collapse = " + "))
  )
)
```



## 4.4 Final Regression Model
```{r final_regrssion_model}
# Select housing facility variables
has_vars <- grep(
  "^has_",
  names(processed_train),
  value = TRUE
)


# Remove selected variables
has_vars <- setdiff(
  has_vars,
  c("has_oil_heating", "has_well_water")
)


# Features used in the refined regression models
base_features <- c(
  "area",
  "building_age",
  "floor",
  "total_floor",
  "walk_1",
  "ward",
  "layout_grouped",
  "building_structure",
  has_vars,
  "stove_installable",
  "stove_type",
  "burner_count",
  "burner_count_missing",
  "station_1_grouped",
  "walk_2",
  "walk_3",
  "fixed_term",
  "town_grouped_18",
  "parking_status",
  "bicycle_parking_grouped",
  "floor_missing",
  "total_floor_missing"
)


# Final regression model
final_formula <- reformulate(
  c(
    base_features,
    "I(area^2)",
    "I(building_age^2)",
    "area:ward",
    "area:building_age"
  ),
  response = "log(rent)"
)


# Final model
final_model <- lm(
  final_formula,
  data = train_model_df
)
```



# 5. Model Evaluation
## 5.1 Prediction Performance
```{r prediction_performance}
# Store regression models
models <- list(
  Model_1 = model_1,
  Model_2 = model_2,
  Model_3 = model_3,
  Final = final_model
)


# Predict rental prices
predictions <- lapply(
  models,
  predict,
  newdata = valid_model_df
)


# Convert log predictions to JPY
predictions$Final <- exp(predictions$Final)


# Check predictions
stopifnot(
  all(sapply(
    predictions,
    function(x) {
      length(x) == nrow(valid_model_df) &&
        all(is.finite(x))
    }
  ))
)


# RMSE function
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
}


# Compare RMSE
rmse_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  RMSE = sapply(
    predictions,
    function(x) rmse(valid_model_df$rent, x)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  rmse_results,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Validation RMSE Comparison (JPY)"
)
```


## 5.2 Statistical Evaluation
```{r statistical_evaluation}
# Compare initial regression models
AIC(model_1, model_2, model_3)
BIC(model_1, model_2, model_3)


# Adjusted R-squared
sapply(
  models[1:3],
  function(m) summary(m)$adj.r.squared
)


# Partial F-test
anova_results <- anova(model_1, model_2, model_3)

f_test <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("Model 1 vs 2", "Model 2 vs 3"),
  F_value = round(anova_results$F[2:3], 2),
  P_value = format.pval(
    anova_results$`Pr(>F)`[2:3],
    digits = 3,
    eps = 0.0001
  )
)

knitr::kable(f_test)
```


## 5.3 Regression Diagnostics
```{r regression_diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(final_model)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
The diagnostic plots suggest deviations from residual normality and possible heteroscedasticity, particularly for higher fitted values.

Several observations also exhibit unusually large residuals or high leverage.



# 6. Competition Submission
```{r final_submission_prediction}
# Prepare full training and test data
submission_data <- prepare_cv_data(
  processed_train,
  processed_test
)

full_train_df <- submission_data$train
test_model_df <- submission_data$valid


# Retrain multiple regression model
submission_model <- lm(
  final_formula,
  data = full_train_df
)


# Predict using the regression model
pred_regression <- exp(
  predict(submission_model, newdata = test_model_df)
)


# Create submission
submission_regression <- data.frame(
  id = sample_submit$V1,
  rent = pred_regression[
    match(sample_submit$V1, test_model_df$id)
  ]
)


# Validate submission
stopifnot(
  nrow(submission_regression) == nrow(sample_submit),
  !anyNA(submission_regression),
  all(is.finite(submission_regression$rent)),
  all(submission_regression$rent > 0),
  anyDuplicated(submission_regression$id) == 0
)


# Save submission without column headers
write.table(
  submission_regression,
  file = "submission_regression.csv",
  sep = ",",
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)

cat("Submission file saved successfully.\n")
```



# 7. Competition Result and Conclusion
The final regression model achieved an RMSE of **22,658.98** JPY on the SIGNATE competition evaluation dataset.

Residual diagnostics revealed some limitations, suggesting opportunities for further improvement in predictive performance.

These findings motivated the use of machine learning models in the subsequent analysis.
